function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization that gives one party (the *mandator*) permission to act on behalf of another party (the *mandatee*). In practice it’s often used in finance and business to allow a customer to grant a bank, service provider, or partner the right to initiate payments, manage accounts, or perform certain actions on their behalf. Key points: | Aspect | Typical meaning | |--------|-----------------| | **Purpose** | Grants authority to execute specific tasks (e.g., direct debits, account management) | | **Parties involved** | Mandator (the person giving the authority) and Mandatee (the entity receiving the authority) | | **Common contexts** | Direct debit agreements, standing orders, subscription services, corporate banking authorizations | | **Lifecycle states** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable
• **Pending** – awaiting confirmation or activation
• **Inactive** – expired, cancelled, or revoked | In many banking APIs, you’ll see endpoints like `partner_mandates` or `user_mandates` that let you query mandates by status (`active`, `pending`, `inactive`). These help partners and users track which authorizations are in effect, waiting to be activated, or have been terminated.
